source.text: וַיִּ֨מְלָךְ־מֶ֔לֶךְ צִדְקִיָּ֖הוּ בֶּן־יֹֽאשִׁיָּ֑הוּ תַּ֗חַת כָּנְיָ֨הוּ֙ בֶּן־יְה֣וֹיָקִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִמְלִ֛יךְ נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֥ר מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֖ל בְּאֶ֥רֶץ יְהוּדָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And reigned king Zedekiah son of Josiah in place of Coniah son of Jehoiakim, whom made king Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon in [the] land of Judah.

en.L: And King Zedekiah son of Josiah reigned in place of Coniah son of Jehoiakim, whom Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon had made king in the land of Judah.
en.B: Zedekiah son of Josiah reigned as king in place of Coniah son of Jehoiakim. Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon had made him king in the land of Judah.
en.R: Zedekiah son of Josiah became king of Judah in place of Coniah son of Jehoiakim. It was Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon who put him on the throne.

es.L: Y reinó el rey Sedequías hijo de Josías en lugar de Conías hijo de Joacim, a quien Nabucodorosor rey de Babilonia había hecho rey en la tierra de Judá.
es.B: Sedequías hijo de Josías reinó como rey en lugar de Conías hijo de Joacim. Nabucodorosor, rey de Babilonia, lo había puesto por rey en la tierra de Judá.
es.R: Sedequías hijo de Josías llegó a ser rey de Judá en lugar de Conías hijo de Joacim. Fue Nabucodorosor, rey de Babilonia, quien lo puso en el trono.

sw.L: Naye mfalme Sedekia mwana wa Yosia akatawala mahali pa Konia mwana wa Yehoyakimu, ambaye Nebukadreza mfalme wa Babeli alimfanya kuwa mfalme katika nchi ya Yuda.
sw.B: Sedekia mwana wa Yosia alitawala kama mfalme mahali pa Konia mwana wa Yehoyakimu. Nebukadreza mfalme wa Babeli ndiye aliyemfanya kuwa mfalme katika nchi ya Yuda.
sw.R: Sedekia mwana wa Yosia akawa mfalme wa Yuda mahali pa Konia mwana wa Yehoyakimu. Nebukadreza mfalme wa Babeli ndiye aliyemweka kwenye kiti cha enzi.

decisions.choice: Coniah son of Jehoiakim: the king also called Jehoiachin and Jeconiah
decisions.reason: He reigned three months and was taken to Babylon in 597 BC (2 Kings 24:8-15). Jeremiah calls him Coniah in 22:24, 28 and here, and Jeconiah in 24:1 and 27:20; Kings calls him Jehoiachin. This verse uses the form Coniah. It is one man under three forms of his name.

decisions.choice: Zedekiah son of Josiah, set on the throne by the king of Babylon
decisions.reason: Zedekiah was a son of Josiah and the uncle of Coniah. Nebuchadrezzar made him king in Coniah's place and changed his name from Mattaniah (2 Kings 24:17). He was Judah's last king. This verse uses the form Nebuchadrezzar, as most of Jeremiah does; it is the same king as Nebuchadnezzar (see 21:2).

decisions.choice: a new section of the book begins here
decisions.reason: Chapter 36 is set in the reign of Jehoiakim. This verse moves the story on to Zedekiah's reign and opens the account of Jeremiah's arrest and imprisonment, which runs to the fall of the city in chapter 39. The book is not arranged in time order.

decisions.choice: reigned as king (B); became king ... It was Nebuchadrezzar ... who put him on the throne (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "and King Zedekiah reigned". Balanced keeps the title in "as king"; Readable splits the long sentence and puts the point last: the king of Babylon chose him.

decisions.choice: Conías
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses the short form of the king's name here, as in 22:24; each verse keeps the form its Hebrew uses (Jeconías, Conías, Joaquín).

decisions.choice: "Konia", the short form this verse uses
decisions.reason: Each verse keeps the form of the king's name its Hebrew uses; the meaning decision says he is the king also called Jehoiachin and Jeconiah.

source.text: וְלֹ֥א שָׁמַ֛ע ה֥וּא וַעֲבָדָ֖יו וְעַ֣ם הָאָ֑רֶץ אֶל־דִּבְרֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֔ר בְּיַ֖ד יִרְמְיָ֥הוּ הַנָּבִֽיא׃

records.literal_gloss: And not listened he and his servants and [the] people of the land to [the] words of Yahweh which he spoke by [the] hand of Jeremiah the prophet.

en.L: And neither he nor his servants nor the people of the land listened to the words of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke by the hand of Jeremiah the prophet.
en.B: But neither he nor his officials nor the people of the land paid attention to the words {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke through the prophet Jeremiah.
en.R: But Zedekiah would not listen to the messages {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave through the prophet Jeremiah. His officials and the people of the land would not listen either.

es.L: Y no escucharon, ni él ni sus siervos ni el pueblo de la tierra, las palabras {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} habló por mano de Jeremías el profeta.
es.B: Pero ni él ni sus funcionarios ni el pueblo de la tierra hicieron caso de las palabras que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} habló por medio del profeta Jeremías.
es.R: Pero Sedequías no quiso escuchar los mensajes que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dio por medio del profeta Jeremías. Tampoco quisieron escucharlos sus funcionarios ni el pueblo del país.

sw.L: Wala yeye, wala watumishi wake, wala watu wa nchi hawakuyasikiliza maneno ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliyoyasema kwa mkono wa Yeremia nabii.
sw.B: Lakini yeye, maafisa wake na watu wa nchi hawakuyajali maneno ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliyasema kupitia nabii Yeremia.
sw.R: Lakini Sedekia hakutaka kusikiliza jumbe ambazo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alizitoa kupitia nabii Yeremia. Maafisa wake na watu wa nchi nao hawakutaka kusikiliza.

decisions.choice: by the hand of Jeremiah: through Jeremiah, with Jeremiah as the messenger
decisions.reason: "By the hand of" a person means by means of that person. The words are the LORD's; Jeremiah is the one who delivered them.

decisions.choice: the people of the land: the citizens of Judah
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean the landowning citizens who had a voice in public life (2 Kings 23:30) or, more widely, the population of Judah. Here it stands beside the king and his officials: the whole nation, from the top down, refused to listen.

decisions.choice: the verse sums up Zedekiah's reign before the story begins
decisions.reason: The verdict comes first. What follows shows a king who asks Jeremiah for prayer and for a word from the LORD (verses 3, 17) but does not act on what he hears.

decisions.choice: servants (L); officials (B, R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for a king's court officials: "servants" at Literal, "officials" at Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: two sentences, with Zedekiah named
decisions.reason: Readable names the king for "he" and gives the officials and the people a sentence of their own, to keep the sentences short.

decisions.choice: siervos (L); funcionarios (B, R)
decisions.reason: A king's servants who hold office are "siervos" at Literal and "funcionarios" at Balanced and Readable, as published Kings.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַח֩ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ צִדְקִיָּ֜הוּ אֶת־יְהוּכַ֣ל בֶּן־שֶֽׁלֶמְיָ֗ה וְאֶת־צְפַנְיָ֤הוּ בֶן־מַֽעֲשֵׂיָה֙ הַכֹּהֵ֔ן אֶל־יִרְמְיָ֥הוּ הַנָּבִ֖יא לֵאמֹ֑ר הִתְפַּלֶּל־נָ֣א בַעֲדֵ֔נוּ אֶל־יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And sent the king Zedekiah Jehucal son of Shelemiah and Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest to Jeremiah the prophet, saying: Pray please on behalf of us to Yahweh our God.

en.L: And King Zedekiah sent Jehucal son of Shelemiah and Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest to Jeremiah the prophet, saying, "Please pray on our behalf to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God."
en.B: King Zedekiah sent Jehucal son of Shelemiah and the priest Zephaniah son of Maaseiah to the prophet Jeremiah with this request: "Please pray to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God for us."
en.R: King Zedekiah sent two men to the prophet Jeremiah: Jehucal son of Shelemiah and the priest Zephaniah son of Maaseiah. They said, "Please pray to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God for us."

es.L: Y envió el rey Sedequías a Jucal hijo de Selemías y a Sofonías hijo de Maasías, el sacerdote, a Jeremías el profeta, diciendo: «Ora, por favor, por nosotros {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} nuestro Dios».
es.B: El rey Sedequías envió a Jucal hijo de Selemías y al sacerdote Sofonías hijo de Maasías al profeta Jeremías con este pedido: «Por favor, ora por nosotros {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} nuestro Dios».
es.R: El rey Sedequías envió a dos hombres al profeta Jeremías: Jucal hijo de Selemías y el sacerdote Sofonías hijo de Maasías. Le dijeron: «Por favor, ora {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} nuestro Dios por nosotros».

sw.L: Naye mfalme Sedekia akamtuma Yehukali mwana wa Shelemia, na Sefania mwana wa Maaseya kuhani, kwa Yeremia nabii, kusema, "Tafadhali utuombee kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wetu."
sw.B: Mfalme Sedekia alimtuma Yehukali mwana wa Shelemia na kuhani Sefania mwana wa Maaseya kwa nabii Yeremia na ombi hili: "Tafadhali utuombee kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wetu."
sw.R: Mfalme Sedekia aliwatuma watu wawili kwa nabii Yeremia: Yehukali mwana wa Shelemia na kuhani Sefania mwana wa Maaseya. Wakasema, "Tafadhali utuombee kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wetu."

decisions.choice: Jehucal son of Shelemiah: a royal official, the Jucal of 38:1
decisions.reason: In 38:1 "Jucal son of Shelemiah", a shorter form of the same name, is one of the officials who ask for Jeremiah's death. The king's messenger here later becomes one of the prophet's enemies.

decisions.choice: Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest
decisions.reason: "The priest" belongs to Zephaniah, as in 21:1. He was a senior priest in the temple (29:25-29) and was among those taken and killed when the city fell (52:24-27).

decisions.choice: pray on our behalf: a request for the prophet to intercede
decisions.reason: The king asks Jeremiah to plead with God for the city, as Hezekiah asked Isaiah when Jerusalem was threatened a century before (Isaiah 37:2-4). Earlier the LORD had told Jeremiah not to pray for this people (7:16; 11:14; 14:11). A similar request is told in 21:1-2.

decisions.choice: sent two men ... They said
decisions.reason: Readable names the messengers after saying how many there were, and turns "saying" into a sentence of its own.

source.text: וְיִרְמְיָ֕הוּ בָּ֥א וְיֹצֵ֖א בְּת֣וֹךְ הָעָ֑ם וְלֹֽא־נָתְנ֥וּ אֹת֖וֹ בֵּ֥ית הַכְּלֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: And Jeremiah [was] coming and going out in [the] midst of the people, and not they had put him [in the] house of the imprisonment.

en.L: Now Jeremiah was coming and going out among the people, and they had not put him in the house of imprisonment.
en.B: At that time Jeremiah was still coming and going among the people; he had not yet been put in prison.
en.R: At that time Jeremiah could still move about freely among the people. He had not been put in prison yet.

es.L: Y Jeremías entraba y salía en medio del pueblo, pues no lo habían puesto en la casa de la cárcel.
es.B: En ese tiempo Jeremías todavía entraba y salía entre el pueblo; aún no lo habían metido en la cárcel.
es.R: En ese tiempo Jeremías todavía podía andar libremente entre la gente. Aún no lo habían metido en la cárcel.

sw.L: Naye Yeremia alikuwa akiingia na kutoka katikati ya watu, kwa maana hawakuwa wamemtia katika nyumba ya kifungo.
sw.B: Wakati huo Yeremia alikuwa bado akiingia na kutoka kati ya watu; alikuwa bado hajatiwa gerezani.
sw.R: Wakati huo Yeremia alikuwa bado anaweza kwenda popote kati ya watu. Alikuwa bado hajafungwa gerezani.

decisions.choice: coming and going out: moving about freely
decisions.reason: "Coming in and going out" describes ordinary life and freedom of movement. Jeremiah was not yet under arrest, as he had been in hiding in 36:26.

decisions.choice: a note of background that looks ahead
decisions.reason: The verse breaks into the story to say how things stood. Its "not yet" prepares for verses 15-16, where he is put in prison.

decisions.choice: the house of imprisonment: the reading the scribes noted in the margin
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew text spells this word slightly differently from the form the scribes noted in the margin to be read aloud. The meaning is the same either way: confinement, prison.

decisions.choice: still ... not yet (B); still ... freely ... yet (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "they had not put him"; "still" and "yet" make clear that his imprisonment comes later in the chapter.

source.text: וְחֵ֥יל פַּרְעֹ֖ה יָצָ֣א מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם וַיִּשְׁמְע֨וּ הַכַּשְׂדִּ֜ים הַצָּרִ֤ים עַל־יְרוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ אֶת־שִׁמְעָ֔ם וַיֵּ֣עָל֔וּ מֵעַ֖ל יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And [the] army of Pharaoh had come out from Egypt; and heard the Chaldeans who [were] besieging Jerusalem the report of them, and they went up from on Jerusalem.

en.L: And the army of Pharaoh had come out of Egypt; and the Chaldeans who were besieging Jerusalem heard the report about them, and they went up from against Jerusalem.
en.B: Pharaoh's army had marched out of Egypt. The Chaldeans besieging Jerusalem heard the news about them and withdrew from the city.
en.R: Meanwhile Pharaoh's army had marched out of Egypt. When the Babylonians who were surrounding Jerusalem heard about it, they pulled back from the city.

es.L: Y el ejército del faraón había salido de Egipto; y los caldeos que sitiaban Jerusalén oyeron la noticia de ellos, y se retiraron de Jerusalén.
es.B: El ejército del faraón había salido de Egipto. Cuando los caldeos que sitiaban Jerusalén oyeron la noticia, se retiraron de la ciudad.
es.R: Mientras tanto, el ejército del faraón había salido de Egipto. Cuando los babilonios que rodeaban Jerusalén se enteraron, se retiraron de la ciudad.

sw.L: Nalo jeshi la Farao lilikuwa limetoka Misri; nao Wakaldayo waliokuwa wakiuzingira Yerusalemu walisikia habari zao, wakaondoka kutoka Yerusalemu.
sw.B: Jeshi la Farao lilikuwa limetoka Misri. Wakaldayo waliokuwa wakiuzingira Yerusalemu waliposikia habari zao, wakaondoka kutoka mji huo.
sw.R: Wakati huo jeshi la Farao lilikuwa limetoka Misri. Wababeli waliokuwa wameuzunguka Yerusalemu waliposikia habari hiyo, waliondoka kutoka mji huo.

decisions.choice: the army of Pharaoh: an Egyptian force sent to help Judah, about 588 BC
decisions.reason: Zedekiah had looked to Egypt for help in his revolt against Babylon (Ezekiel 17:15). The Pharaoh is not named here; the Pharaoh of this time was Hophra, named in 44:30. The help came to nothing (verse 7; Lamentations 4:17).

decisions.choice: the Chaldeans: the Babylonians
decisions.reason: The Chaldeans were the people of southern Mesopotamia whose dynasty ruled Babylon at this time. In Jeremiah the name means the Babylonian army and nation (see 21:4).

decisions.choice: went up from against Jerusalem: lifted the siege and withdrew
decisions.reason: An army that "goes up from" a city it is attacking marches away from it, here to meet the Egyptians. The words answer the king's hope in 21:2, but only for a time (verse 8).

decisions.choice: the verse gives the background to the king's request
decisions.reason: The verbs are best read as describing what had already happened when Zedekiah sent to Jeremiah: the siege had been lifted, and the city was hoping it would not return.

decisions.choice: the Babylonians
decisions.reason: As in Isaiah and the rest of Jeremiah, Readable says "Babylonians" for "Chaldeans".

decisions.choice: los babilonios
decisions.reason: Readable names the Chaldeans by their better-known name, as in this chapter throughout.

source.text: וַֽיְהִי֙ דְּבַר־יְהוָ֔ה אֶל־יִרְמְיָ֥הוּ הַנָּבִ֖יא לֵאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And came [the] word of Yahweh to Jeremiah the prophet, saying:

en.L: And the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Jeremiah the prophet, saying:
en.B: Then the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to the prophet Jeremiah:
en.R: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave the prophet Jeremiah this message:

es.L: Y vino la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} a Jeremías el profeta, diciendo:
es.B: Entonces la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} vino al profeta Jeremías:
es.R: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dio al profeta Jeremías este mensaje:

sw.L: Ndipo neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} likamjia Yeremia nabii, kusema:
sw.B: Kisha neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} likamjia nabii Yeremia:
sw.R: Kisha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akampa nabii Yeremia ujumbe huu:

decisions.choice: the LORD's answer to the king's request
decisions.reason: The word that follows (verses 7-10) is the reply Jeremiah is to send back to Zedekiah through his messengers.

decisions.choice: the word of the LORD came to ..., saying (L); the word of the LORD came to ... (B); the LORD gave ... this message (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this formula throughout Jeremiah.

source.text: כֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כֹּ֤התֹֽאמְרוּ֙ אֶל־מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה הַשֹּׁלֵ֧חַ אֶתְכֶ֛ם אֵלַ֖י לְדָרְשֵׁ֑נִי הִנֵּ֣ה׀חֵ֣יל פַּרְעֹ֗ה הַיֹּצֵ֤א לָכֶם֙ לְעֶזְרָ֔ה שָׁ֥ב לְאַרְצ֖וֹ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus says Yahweh, [the] God of Israel: Thus you will say to [the] king of Judah who sent you to me to inquire of me: Look, [the] army of Pharaoh which [is] coming out to you for help [is] returning to its land, Egypt.

en.L: "Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel: Thus you shall say to the king of Judah, who sent you to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to inquire of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}: 'Look, the army of Pharaoh that is coming out to help you is returning to its own land, Egypt.
en.B: "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says this: Tell the king of Judah, who sent you to seek {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} answer: 'Pharaoh's army, which has set out to help you, is going back to its own land, to Egypt.
en.R: "This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says: The king of Judah sent you to ask what I have to say. Give him this answer: 'Pharaoh's army marched out to help you, but it is going back home to Egypt.

es.L: «Así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios de Israel: Así {{plural_you:dirán|diréis}} al rey de Judá, que {{plural_you:los|os}} envió a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} para consultar{{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}: “He aquí, el ejército del faraón que salió en {{plural_you:su ayuda|vuestra ayuda}} se vuelve a su tierra, a Egipto.
es.B: «{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios de Israel, dice esto: {{plural_you:Díganle|Decidle}} al rey de Judá, que {{plural_you:los|os}} envió a pedir {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} respuesta: “El ejército del faraón, que salió para {{plural_you:ayudarlos|ayudaros}}, se vuelve a su tierra, a Egipto.
es.R: «Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios de Israel: El rey de Judá {{plural_you:los|os}} envió a preguntar lo que yo tengo que decir. {{plural_you:Denle|Dadle}} esta respuesta: “El ejército del faraón salió para {{plural_you:ayudarlos|ayudaros}}, pero se vuelve a su tierra, a Egipto.

sw.L: "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asema hivi, Mungu wa Israeli: Hivi ndivyo mtakavyomwambia mfalme wa Yuda, aliyewatuma {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}} kuniuliza: 'Tazama, jeshi la Farao lililotoka kuja kuwasaidia linarudi katika nchi yake, Misri.
sw.B: "Hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, asemavyo: Mwambieni mfalme wa Yuda, aliyewatuma kutafuta jibu {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}: 'Jeshi la Farao, lililotoka kuja kuwasaidia, linarudi katika nchi yake, Misri.
sw.R: "Hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, analosema: Mfalme wa Yuda aliwatuma kuuliza nina la kusema. Mpeni jibu hili: 'Jeshi la Farao lilitoka kuja kuwasaidia, lakini linarudi nyumbani Misri.

decisions.choice: inquire of me: seek a word from God through a prophet
decisions.reason: The verb means to seek, and with God as its object it means asking for his answer in a crisis (21:2; 1 Kings 22:8). The messengers had asked for prayer (verse 3); the LORD treats the request as a question about what will happen.

decisions.choice: you: the king's messengers
decisions.reason: "You shall say" and "sent you" are plural. Jeremiah is to give the answer to Jehucal and Zephaniah to carry back.

decisions.choice: is returning: certain, though it has not yet happened
decisions.reason: The verb is in a form that usually describes a completed act. Here it states the future as already settled: the Egyptian army that has just set out will go home without saving the city.

decisions.choice: sent you to ask what I have to say. Give him this answer:
decisions.reason: Readable splits the sentence and makes clear that what follows is the LORD's reply to the king.

decisions.choice: double quotes for the LORD's word; single quotes for the message to the king
decisions.reason: The word of the LORD to Jeremiah runs from here to the end of verse 10. The message the messengers are to take to the king is quoted inside it.

decisions.choice: plural_you for the messengers and for the king and his people
decisions.reason: "You" is plural throughout: first the two men sent to Jeremiah, then the king with Jerusalem, whom Pharaoh came to help.

decisions.choice: double quotes for the LORD's word to Jeremiah, single quotes for the message to the king, as the English
decisions.reason: The narrative frame quotes speech as prose does; "ninyi" (plural) addresses the king's two messengers.

records.literal_gloss: And will return the Chaldeans and fight against the city this, and capture it and burn it with fire.

en.L: And the Chaldeans will return and fight against this city, and they will capture it and burn it with fire.
en.B: Then the Chaldeans will come back and attack this city. They will capture it and set it on fire.
en.R: Then the Babylonians will come back and attack this city. They will capture it and burn it down.

es.L: Y volverán los caldeos y pelearán contra esta ciudad, y la tomarán y la quemarán con fuego.
es.B: Entonces los caldeos volverán y atacarán esta ciudad. La tomarán y le prenderán fuego.
es.R: Entonces los babilonios volverán y atacarán esta ciudad. La conquistarán y la quemarán por completo.

sw.L: Nao Wakaldayo watarudi, na kupigana na mji huu, nao watautwaa na kuuteketeza kwa moto.
sw.B: Kisha Wakaldayo watarudi na kuushambulia mji huu. Watautwaa na kuuchoma moto.
sw.R: Kisha Wababeli watarudi na kuushambulia mji huu. Watauteka na kuuchoma moto kabisa.

decisions.choice: capture it and burn it: what happened in 587 BC
decisions.reason: The city was taken and burned when the siege resumed (39:2, 8; 52:7, 13). The same words are spoken of the city in 21:10; 32:29; 34:22.

decisions.choice: the Chaldeans' withdrawal is only for a time
decisions.reason: "Will return" answers "is returning" in verse 7: as the Egyptians go back home, the Babylonians come back to the siege.

decisions.choice: the Babylonians
decisions.reason: As in Isaiah and the rest of Jeremiah, Readable says "Babylonians" for "Chaldeans".

source.text: כֹּ֣ה׀אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה אַל־תַּשִּׁ֤אוּ נַפְשֹֽׁתֵיכֶם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הָלֹ֛ךְ יֵלְכ֥וּ מֵעָלֵ֖ינוּ הַכַּשְׂדִּ֑ים כִּי־לֹ֖א יֵלֵֽכוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus says Yahweh: Do not deceive your selves, saying: Surely will go from on us the Chaldeans; for not they will go.

en.L: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: Do not deceive yourselves, saying, "The Chaldeans will surely go away from us," for they will not go.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: Do not fool yourselves by thinking, "The Chaldeans are sure to leave us for good." They will not leave.
en.R: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: Do not fool yourselves. Do not tell yourselves, "The Babylonians are going away for good." They are not going away.

es.L: Así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: No {{plural_you:se engañen|os engañéis}} a {{plural_you:ustedes mismos|vosotros mismos}}, diciendo: ‘Ciertamente los caldeos se irán de nosotros’, porque no se irán.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dice esto: No {{plural_you:se engañen|os engañéis}} pensando: ‘Los caldeos se van a ir de aquí para siempre’. No se irán.
es.R: Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: No {{plural_you:se engañen|os engañéis}}. No {{plural_you:se digan|os digáis}}: ‘Los babilonios se van para siempre’. No se van a ir.

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asema hivi: Msijidanganye nafsi zenu, mkisema, "Hakika Wakaldayo wataondoka kwetu," kwa maana hawataondoka.
sw.B: Hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asemavyo: Msijidanganye mkidhani, "Hakika Wakaldayo wataondoka kwetu kabisa." Hawataondoka.
sw.R: Hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} analosema: Msijidanganye. Msiseme mioyoni mwenu, "Wababeli wanaondoka kabisa." Hawaondoki.

decisions.choice: do not deceive yourselves
decisions.reason: The verb means to mislead or delude, and "your souls" means your own selves. The people are deceiving themselves with a false hope (compare 29:8).

decisions.choice: surely go ... they will not go
decisions.reason: The Hebrew doubles the verb for emphasis: "going they will go", that is, they are certainly leaving. The LORD answers with the same verb: they will not go.

decisions.choice: you: the king and the people of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The verbs are plural. The warning is for everyone in the city who has taken the lifting of the siege as the end of the danger.

decisions.choice: leave us for good (B); going away for good (R)
decisions.reason: The Babylonians had already left for a time (verse 5). "For good" makes clear that the false hope is that they will never come back.

decisions.choice: the Babylonians
decisions.reason: As in Isaiah and the rest of Jeremiah, Readable says "Babylonians" for "Chaldeans".

source.text: כִּ֣י אִם־הִכִּיתֶ֞ם כָּל־חֵ֤יל כַּשְׂדִּים֙ הַנִּלְחָמִ֣ים אִתְּכֶ֔ם וְנִ֨שְׁאֲרוּ בָ֔ם אֲנָשִׁ֖ים מְדֻקָּרִ֑ים אִ֤ישׁ בְּאָהֳלוֹ֙ יָק֔וּמוּ וְשָֽׂרְפ֛וּ אֶת־הָעִ֥יר הַזֹּ֖את בָּאֵֽשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: For even if you struck down all [the] army of [the] Chaldeans who [are] fighting with you, and remained among them men pierced through, each in his tent, they would rise and burn the city this with fire.

en.L: For even if you struck down the whole army of the Chaldeans who are fighting against you, and there remained among them [only] men pierced through, each in his tent, they would rise up and burn this city with fire.'"
en.B: Even if you were to defeat the entire Chaldean army that is fighting against you, and only badly wounded men were left among them, each lying in his tent, they would still get up and burn this city down.'"
en.R: Suppose you defeated the whole Babylonian army that is fighting against you, and only wounded men were left, lying in their tents. Even those men would get up and burn this city to the ground.'"

es.L: Porque aunque {{plural_you:derrotaran|derrotarais}} a todo el ejército de los caldeos que pelean contra {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, y quedaran entre ellos [solo] hombres traspasados, cada uno en su tienda, se levantarían y quemarían esta ciudad con fuego”».
es.B: Aunque {{plural_you:derrotaran|derrotarais}} a todo el ejército caldeo que pelea contra {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, y entre ellos solo quedaran hombres gravemente heridos, cada uno tendido en su tienda, aun así se levantarían y quemarían esta ciudad”».
es.R: Supongamos que {{plural_you:derrotaran|derrotarais}} a todo el ejército babilonio que pelea contra {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, y solo quedaran hombres heridos, tendidos en sus tiendas. Aun esos hombres se levantarían y quemarían esta ciudad hasta los cimientos”».

sw.L: Kwa maana hata kama mngelipiga jeshi lote la Wakaldayo wanaopigana nanyi, wakabaki miongoni mwao [watu tu] waliochomwa, kila mtu katika hema yake, wangeinuka na kuuteketeza mji huu kwa moto.'"
sw.B: Hata kama mngelishinda jeshi lote la Wakaldayo linalopigana nanyi, na wakabaki kati yao watu waliojeruhiwa vibaya tu, kila mmoja amelala katika hema yake, bado wangeinuka na kuuchoma moto mji huu.'"
sw.R: Tuseme mmelishinda jeshi lote la Wababeli linalopigana nanyi, na wamebaki watu waliojeruhiwa tu, wamelala katika hema zao. Hata watu hao wangeinuka na kuuchoma mji huu mpaka ukateketea kabisa.'"

decisions.choice: even if: a supposition that will not happen
decisions.reason: The LORD imagines the best that Judah could hope for, a complete victory, only to say that even then the city would fall. It is not a promise that Judah will win any battle.

decisions.choice: men pierced through: the badly wounded, unable to fight
decisions.reason: The word describes men stabbed or run through by a weapon (the same verb is used in Zechariah 12:10). Men left lying in their tents are the weakest part of a beaten army.

decisions.choice: the city's fall does not depend on the strength of armies
decisions.reason: The point is that the LORD has decided Jerusalem's fate (verse 8). Even crippled men would be enough to carry out his judgment.

decisions.choice: [only] (L); only ... still (B); only ... Even those men (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says that wounded men remained; the sense is that nothing else remained. Literal brackets "only"; Balanced and Readable add words that bring out the contrast.

decisions.choice: the Babylonians
decisions.reason: As in Isaiah and the rest of Jeremiah, Readable says "Babylonians" for "Chaldeans".

source.text: וְהָיָ֗ה בְּהֵֽעָלוֹת֙ חֵ֣יל הַכַּשְׂדִּ֔ים מֵעַ֖ל יְרֽוּשָׁלִָ֑ם מִפְּנֵ֖י חֵ֥יל פַּרְעֹֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when had gone up [the] army of the Chaldeans from on Jerusalem from before [the] army of Pharaoh,

en.L: And it happened, when the army of the Chaldeans had gone up from against Jerusalem because of the army of Pharaoh,
en.B: When the Chaldean army had withdrawn from Jerusalem because Pharaoh's army was approaching,
en.R: The Babylonian army had pulled back from Jerusalem because Pharaoh's army was coming.

es.L: Y sucedió que, cuando el ejército de los caldeos se retiró de Jerusalén a causa del ejército del faraón,
es.B: Cuando el ejército caldeo se retiró de Jerusalén porque se acercaba el ejército del faraón,
es.R: El ejército babilonio se había retirado de Jerusalén porque venía el ejército del faraón.

sw.L: Ikawa, jeshi la Wakaldayo lilipokuwa limeondoka kutoka Yerusalemu kwa sababu ya jeshi la Farao,
sw.B: Jeshi la Wakaldayo lilipokuwa limeondoka Yerusalemu kwa sababu jeshi la Farao lilikuwa likikaribia,
sw.R: Jeshi la Wababeli lilikuwa limeondoka Yerusalemu kwa sababu jeshi la Farao lilikuwa likija.

decisions.choice: a time clause that leads into verse 12
decisions.reason: The sentence continues into the next verse: what Jeremiah did happened during the pause in the siege described in verse 5.

decisions.choice: from before the army of Pharaoh: because of it, to face it
decisions.reason: "From before" someone often gives the reason for leaving: the Babylonians broke off the siege on account of the Egyptian army.

decisions.choice: because Pharaoh's army was approaching (B); was coming (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew names only the army; Balanced and Readable add the verb that the setting implies (verse 5). Readable makes this verse a sentence of its own.

decisions.choice: the Babylonians
decisions.reason: As in Isaiah and the rest of Jeremiah, Readable says "Babylonians" for "Chaldeans".

source.text: וַיֵּצֵ֤א יִרְמְיָ֨הוּ֙ מִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם לָלֶ֖כֶת אֶ֣רֶץ בִּנְיָמִ֑ן לַחֲלִ֥ק מִשָּׁ֖ם בְּת֥וֹךְ הָעָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: and went out Jeremiah from Jerusalem to go [to the] land of Benjamin, to receive a share from there in [the] midst of the people.

en.L: Jeremiah went out from Jerusalem to go to the land of Benjamin, to receive a share from there among the people.
en.B: Jeremiah set out from Jerusalem to go to the land of Benjamin, to receive his share of property there among the people.
en.R: During that time Jeremiah left Jerusalem to go to the land of Benjamin. He wanted to receive his share of family land there among the people.

es.L: salió Jeremías de Jerusalén para ir a la tierra de Benjamín, para recibir de allí una porción en medio del pueblo.
es.B: Jeremías salió de Jerusalén para ir a la tierra de Benjamín, a recibir allí su parte de una propiedad entre el pueblo.
es.R: En ese tiempo Jeremías salió de Jerusalén para ir a la tierra de Benjamín. Quería recibir allí la parte de la tierra de su familia que le correspondía.

sw.L: Yeremia akatoka Yerusalemu ili aende nchi ya Benyamini, kupokea fungu lake huko katikati ya watu.
sw.B: Yeremia aliondoka Yerusalemu kwenda nchi ya Benyamini, ili kupokea sehemu yake ya mali huko kati ya watu.
sw.R: Wakati huo Yeremia aliondoka Yerusalemu kwenda nchi ya Benyamini. Alitaka kupokea sehemu yake ya ardhi ya ukoo huko kati ya watu.

decisions.choice: to receive a share: to take his part of a family inheritance
alternatives: to slip away from there among the people
to divide property there among his relatives
decisions.reason: The verb is rare in this form and its sense here is not certain. It comes from a root meaning to divide or to be given a portion, and is best taken as Jeremiah going to settle his share of family property in his home district; chapter 32 tells how he bought a relative's field at Anathoth in Benjamin (32:6-15). Others take it from a like-sounding root meaning to be smooth and read "to slip away from there among the people", or understand it as dividing property among relatives.

decisions.choice: the land of Benjamin: the tribal land just north of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Jeremiah came from Anathoth, a priests' town in the land of Benjamin a few miles from the city (1:1).

decisions.choice: among the people: in the presence of the people there
decisions.reason: The phrase may mean the people of his home town, before whom the share was settled, or the crowds leaving the city while the siege was lifted.

decisions.choice: his share of property (B); his share of family land (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has only the verb "to receive a share". Balanced and Readable say what kind of share is most likely meant; this follows the uncertain reading in m1.

source.text: וַיְהִי־ה֞וּא בְּשַׁ֣עַר בִּנְיָמִ֗ן וְשָׁם֙ בַּ֣עַל פְּקִדֻ֔ת וּשְׁמוֹ֙ יִרְאִיָּ֔יה בֶּן־שֶֽׁלֶמְיָ֖ה בֶּן־חֲנַנְיָ֑ה וַיִּתְפֹּ֞שׂ אֶֽת־יִרְמְיָ֤הוּ הַנָּבִיא֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר אֶל־הַכַּשְׂדִּ֖ים אַתָּ֥ה נֹפֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And he was at [the] gate of Benjamin, and there [was] a master of [the] guard, and his name [was] Irijah son of Shelemiah son of Hananiah; and he seized Jeremiah the prophet, saying: To the Chaldeans you [are] falling.

en.L: And he was at the Benjamin Gate, and a captain of the guard was there, and his name was Irijah son of Shelemiah son of Hananiah; and he seized Jeremiah the prophet, saying, "You are falling away to the Chaldeans!"
en.B: When he reached the Benjamin Gate, a captain of the guard named Irijah son of Shelemiah, son of Hananiah, was there. He arrested the prophet Jeremiah and said, "You are deserting to the Chaldeans!"
en.R: But when he reached the Benjamin Gate, the officer in charge of the guard stopped him. His name was Irijah son of Shelemiah, son of Hananiah. He arrested the prophet Jeremiah. "You are going over to the Babylonians!" he said.

es.L: Y cuando él estaba en la puerta de Benjamín, estaba allí un capitán de la guardia, cuyo nombre [era] Irías hijo de Selemías, hijo de Hananías; y prendió a Jeremías el profeta, diciendo: «¡Tú te pasas a los caldeos!».
es.B: Cuando llegó a la puerta de Benjamín, estaba allí un capitán de la guardia llamado Irías hijo de Selemías, hijo de Hananías. Él arrestó al profeta Jeremías y le dijo: «¡Te estás pasando a los caldeos!».
es.R: Pero cuando llegó a la puerta de Benjamín, el oficial encargado de la guardia lo detuvo. Se llamaba Irías hijo de Selemías, hijo de Hananías. Arrestó al profeta Jeremías y le dijo: «¡Te vas a pasar al lado de los babilonios!».

sw.L: Naye alipokuwa katika Lango la Benyamini, mkuu wa walinzi alikuwako huko, jina lake Iria mwana wa Shelemia mwana wa Hanania; naye akamkamata Yeremia nabii, kusema, "Unakimbilia kwa Wakaldayo!"
sw.B: Alipofika kwenye Lango la Benyamini, mkuu wa walinzi aitwaye Iria mwana wa Shelemia, mwana wa Hanania, alikuwa huko. Akamkamata nabii Yeremia, akasema, "Unawakimbilia Wakaldayo!"
sw.R: Lakini alipofika kwenye Lango la Benyamini, afisa aliyesimamia walinzi akamzuia. Jina lake lilikuwa Iria mwana wa Shelemia, mwana wa Hanania. Akamkamata nabii Yeremia, akasema, "Unajiunga na Wababeli!"

decisions.choice: the Benjamin Gate: a gate on the north side of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The gate took its name from the road north to the land of Benjamin, where Jeremiah was going (38:7; Zechariah 14:10). It is the city gate, not the upper Benjamin Gate of the temple named in 20:2.

decisions.choice: a captain of the guard: the officer in charge of the gate's watch
decisions.reason: The phrase means "master of the oversight", the man responsible for the guard at the gate. It occurs only here.

decisions.choice: falling to the Chaldeans: deserting to the enemy
decisions.reason: To "fall to" an army is to go over to it and give oneself up (21:9; 38:19; 39:9). Jeremiah had urged the people to surrender (21:9), so the charge looked likely. Leaving the city while the enemy was nearby made him a suspect.

decisions.choice: Irijah's grandfather Hananiah
decisions.reason: The text does not say whether this Hananiah is the prophet who opposed Jeremiah in chapter 28. The name was common, and nothing more is known of the family.

decisions.choice: deserting (B); going over to (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew verb "falling"; Balanced and Readable say what it means in this setting. Readable puts the officer's words after the arrest, in the order the reader needs.

decisions.choice: the Babylonians
decisions.reason: As in Isaiah and the rest of Jeremiah, Readable says "Babylonians" for "Chaldeans".

decisions.choice: te pasas (L); te estás pasando (B); te vas a pasar al lado de (R)
decisions.reason: "Falling to" an enemy is going over to his side; Spanish "pasarse a" says it at every level.

decisions.choice: "Unakimbilia kwa Wakaldayo" (L); "Unawakimbilia Wakaldayo" (B); "Unajiunga na Wababeli" (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "fall to" means desert to the enemy; Swahili "kuanguka" would not carry that sense, so every level says "flee to" or "join".

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יִרְמְיָ֜הוּ שֶׁ֗קֶר אֵינֶ֤נִּי נֹפֵל֙ עַל־הַכַּשְׂדִּ֔ים וְלֹ֥א שָׁמַ֖ע אֵלָ֑יו וַיִּתְפֹּ֤שׂ יִרְאִיָּיה֙ בְּיִרְמְיָ֔הוּ וַיְבִאֵ֖הוּ אֶל־הַשָּׂרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Jeremiah: A lie! Not I [am] falling to the Chaldeans. And not he listened to him, and seized Irijah Jeremiah and brought him to the princes.

en.L: And Jeremiah said, "A lie! I am not falling away to the Chaldeans." But he did not listen to him, and Irijah seized Jeremiah and brought him to the princes.
en.B: "That is a lie!" Jeremiah said. "I am not deserting to the Chaldeans." Irijah refused to listen. He arrested Jeremiah and brought him to the officials.
en.R: "That is not true!" Jeremiah answered. "I am not going over to the Babylonians." But Irijah would not listen. He arrested Jeremiah and took him to the leaders.

es.L: Y Jeremías dijo: «¡Mentira! No me paso a los caldeos». Pero no lo escuchó, sino que Irías prendió a Jeremías y lo llevó a los príncipes.
es.B: «¡Eso es mentira!», dijo Jeremías. «No me estoy pasando a los caldeos». Pero Irías no quiso escucharlo. Arrestó a Jeremías y lo llevó ante los jefes.
es.R: «¡Eso no es cierto!», respondió Jeremías. «No me voy a pasar al lado de los babilonios». Pero Irías no le hizo caso. Arrestó a Jeremías y lo llevó ante los dirigentes.

sw.L: Naye Yeremia akasema, "Uongo! Mimi sikimbilii kwa Wakaldayo." Lakini hakumsikiliza; Iria akamkamata Yeremia, akamleta kwa wakuu.
sw.B: Yeremia akasema, "Huo ni uongo! Mimi siwakimbilii Wakaldayo." Lakini Iria alikataa kumsikiliza. Akamkamata Yeremia, akampeleka kwa maafisa.
sw.R: Yeremia akajibu, "Si kweli! Mimi sijiungi na Wababeli." Lakini Iria hakutaka kumsikiliza. Akamkamata Yeremia, akampeleka kwa viongozi.

decisions.choice: A lie!: a flat denial
decisions.reason: The single word means falsehood. Jeremiah answers the charge with one word before he explains.

decisions.choice: the princes: the king's officials under Zedekiah
decisions.reason: Under Jehoiakim some of the court officials had protected Jeremiah (26:16, 24; 36:19). Many leading men had been taken to Babylon with Coniah (2 Kings 24:14-15). The officials who now hear his case treat him as a traitor (38:4).

decisions.choice: princes (L); officials (B); leaders (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this word in Jeremiah (as 26:10). These are the king's chief officers, not his sons.

decisions.choice: the Babylonians
decisions.reason: As in Isaiah and the rest of Jeremiah, Readable says "Babylonians" for "Chaldeans".

source.text: וַיִּקְצְפ֧וּ הַשָּׂרִ֛ים עַֽל־יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ וְהִכּ֣וּ אֹת֑וֹ וְנָתְנ֨וּ אוֹת֜וֹ בֵּ֣ית הָאֵס֗וּר בֵּ֚ית יְהוֹנָתָ֣ן הַסֹּפֵ֔ר כִּֽי־אֹת֥וֹ עָשׂ֖וּ לְבֵ֥ית הַכֶּֽלֶא׃

records.literal_gloss: And were angry the princes at Jeremiah, and they struck him and put him [in the] house of the fetter, [the] house of Jonathan the scribe; for it they had made into [the] house of the prison.

en.L: And the princes were angry with Jeremiah, and they struck him and put him in the house of confinement, the house of Jonathan the secretary, for they had made it into the prison.
en.B: The officials were furious with Jeremiah. They beat him and locked him up in the house of Jonathan the secretary, which they had turned into a prison.
en.R: The leaders were very angry with Jeremiah. They beat him and locked him up in the house of Jonathan, the royal secretary. They had turned his house into a prison.

es.L: Y se enojaron los príncipes contra Jeremías, y lo golpearon y lo pusieron en la casa de prisión, en la casa de Jonatán el escriba, porque la habían convertido en cárcel.
es.B: Los jefes se enfurecieron con Jeremías. Lo golpearon y lo encerraron en la casa de Jonatán el secretario, que habían convertido en cárcel.
es.R: Los dirigentes se enojaron mucho con Jeremías. Lo golpearon y lo encerraron en la casa de Jonatán, el secretario del rey. Habían convertido su casa en una cárcel.

sw.L: Nao wakuu wakamkasirikia Yeremia, wakampiga, wakamtia katika nyumba ya kifungo, nyumba ya Yonathani mwandishi, kwa maana walikuwa wameifanya kuwa gereza.
sw.B: Maafisa walimkasirikia sana Yeremia. Wakampiga, wakamfunga katika nyumba ya Yonathani katibu, ambayo walikuwa wameifanya kuwa gereza.
sw.R: Viongozi walimkasirikia sana Yeremia. Wakampiga, wakamfunga katika nyumba ya Yonathani, katibu wa mfalme. Walikuwa wameifanya nyumba yake kuwa gereza.

decisions.choice: the house of confinement: a place where prisoners were held
decisions.reason: The word comes from a verb meaning to bind; the phrase means a place of detention. It is explained by what follows: a private house that served as a prison.

decisions.choice: Jonathan the secretary: a senior royal official
decisions.reason: The secretary was one of the chief officers of the court, in charge of royal writing and records (36:12; 2 Kings 22:3). This man's house had been made into a jail, perhaps because the regular prison was full or because it could be closely guarded.

decisions.choice: they struck him: a beating as punishment
decisions.reason: The officials have him beaten before the matter is tried, as Pashhur had done in 20:2.

decisions.choice: princes (L); officials (B); leaders (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this word in Jeremiah (as 26:10). These are the king's chief officers, not his sons.

decisions.choice: locked him up in the house of Jonathan ... a prison
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses two words for a prison here; Balanced and Readable say it once, in the place where the house is named, so the sentence does not repeat itself. Readable adds "royal" to show whose secretary he was.

source.text: כִּ֣י בָ֧א יִרְמְיָ֛הוּ אֶל־בֵּ֥ית הַבּ֖וֹר וְאֶל־הַֽחֲנֻ֑יוֹת וַיֵּֽשֶׁב־שָׁ֥ם יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ יָמִ֥ים רַבִּֽים׃פ

records.literal_gloss: For came Jeremiah into [the] house of the cistern and into the vaults, and stayed there Jeremiah many days.

en.L: So Jeremiah came into the cistern house and into the vaults, and Jeremiah stayed there many days.
en.B: So Jeremiah was put in the cistern house, in its vaulted cells, and he stayed there for a long time.
en.R: So Jeremiah was put in a cell in an underground pit, and he stayed there for a long time.

es.L: Así que entró Jeremías en la casa de la cisterna y en las bóvedas, y permaneció allí Jeremías muchos días.
es.B: Así que Jeremías fue metido en la casa de la cisterna, en sus celdas abovedadas, y allí se quedó mucho tiempo.
es.R: Así que metieron a Jeremías en una celda en un pozo bajo tierra, y allí se quedó mucho tiempo.

sw.L: Basi Yeremia akaingia katika nyumba ya birika, ndani ya vyumba vya chini, naye Yeremia akakaa huko siku nyingi.
sw.B: Basi Yeremia akatiwa katika nyumba ya birika, katika vyumba vyake vya chini vyenye matao, naye akakaa huko muda mrefu.
sw.R: Basi Yeremia akatiwa katika chumba ndani ya shimo chini ya ardhi, naye akakaa huko muda mrefu.

decisions.choice: So: the word sums up what verse 15 has told
decisions.reason: The connecting word usually means "for" or "when". Here it gathers up the account of the arrest: this is where Jeremiah ended up.

decisions.choice: the cistern house: an underground pit used as a cell
decisions.reason: The word for cistern is a pit cut in the rock to hold rainwater. Dry or emptied cisterns were used to hold prisoners (Genesis 37:24; 40:15). Jeremiah is later let down into a muddy cistern (38:6).

decisions.choice: the vaults: arched rooms or cells, probably within the cistern house
decisions.reason: The word occurs only here, and its exact sense is uncertain. It is usually linked to a root meaning to bend or to camp, which suggests vaulted or arched rooms. In later Hebrew a related word means a shop or a booth. It may name cells cut into the walls of the pit.

decisions.choice: many days: a long time
decisions.reason: The length is not given. The phrase means a long and uncertain stay.

decisions.choice: was put
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says that Jeremiah "came" into the pit; Balanced and Readable make clear that he was taken there as a prisoner (verse 15).

decisions.choice: a cell in an underground pit
decisions.reason: Readable explains the cistern house and its vaults with simple words. It follows the uncertain sense of m3.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַח֩ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ צִדְקִיָּ֜הוּ וַיִּקָּחֵ֗הוּ וַיִּשְׁאָלֵ֨הוּ הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ בְּבֵיתוֹ֙ בַּסֵּ֔תֶר וַיֹּ֕אמֶר הֲיֵ֥שׁ דָּבָ֖ר מֵאֵ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יִרְמְיָ֨הוּ֙ יֵ֔שׁ וַיֹּ֕אמֶר בְּיַ֥ד מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֖ל תִּנָּתֵֽן׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And sent the king Zedekiah and took him, and asked him the king in his house in secrecy, and said: Is there a word from Yahweh? And said Jeremiah: There is. And he said: Into [the] hand of [the] king of Babylon you will be given.

en.L: Then King Zedekiah sent and took him, and the king asked him secretly in his house and said, "Is there a word from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}?" And Jeremiah said, "There is." And he said, "You will be given into the hand of the king of Babylon."
en.B: Then King Zedekiah sent for him and had him brought to the palace, where he questioned him in private. "Is there any word from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}?" the king asked. "There is," Jeremiah replied. "You will be handed over to the king of Babylon."
en.R: Later King Zedekiah sent for Jeremiah and had him brought to the palace. There the king asked him in secret, "Do you have a message from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}?" "Yes, I do," Jeremiah answered. "You will be handed over to the king of Babylon."

es.L: Entonces el rey Sedequías envió y lo tomó, y el rey le preguntó en secreto en su casa, y dijo: «¿Hay palabra de parte {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}?». Y Jeremías dijo: «La hay». Y dijo: «En mano del rey de Babilonia serás entregado».
es.B: Después el rey Sedequías mandó a buscarlo y lo hizo llevar al palacio, donde lo interrogó en privado. «¿Hay alguna palabra de parte {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}?», preguntó el rey. «La hay», respondió Jeremías. «Serás entregado en manos del rey de Babilonia».
es.R: Más tarde el rey Sedequías mandó a buscar a Jeremías y lo hizo llevar al palacio. Allí el rey le preguntó en secreto: «¿Tienes algún mensaje {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}?». «Sí, lo tengo», respondió Jeremías. «Vas a ser entregado al rey de Babilonia».

sw.L: Kisha mfalme Sedekia akatuma watu, akamtwaa; mfalme akamwuliza kwa siri nyumbani mwake, akasema, "Je, liko neno kutoka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}?" Yeremia akasema, "Liko." Akasema, "Utatiwa mkononi mwa mfalme wa Babeli."
sw.B: Kisha mfalme Sedekia akatuma watu wamlete ikulu, akamwuliza faraghani, "Je, kuna neno lolote kutoka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}?" Yeremia akajibu, "Lipo. Utatiwa mikononi mwa mfalme wa Babeli."
sw.R: Baadaye mfalme Sedekia alituma watu wamlete Yeremia ikulu. Huko mfalme akamwuliza kwa siri, "Je, una ujumbe kutoka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}?" Yeremia akajibu, "Ndiyo, ninao. Utatiwa mikononi mwa mfalme wa Babeli."

decisions.choice: in his house, in secret: in the palace, out of sight of the officials
decisions.reason: The king's "house" is the royal palace. Zedekiah feared his own officials (38:5, 19, 24-26) and could not be seen consulting the man they had jailed as a traitor.

decisions.choice: There is ... And he said: Jeremiah gives a short answer and then the word itself
decisions.reason: Jeremiah first answers the king's question with one word; the second "he said" introduces the message. It is the same message he had given before (21:7; 32:4; 34:3).

decisions.choice: be given into the hand of: be handed over to the power of
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for power and control. Zedekiah will be captured and brought before the king of Babylon (39:5-7).

decisions.choice: sent for him and had him brought to the palace
decisions.reason: "Sent and took him" means he had Jeremiah fetched. Balanced and Readable say so and name the place from "in his house".

decisions.choice: Yes, I do
decisions.reason: The Hebrew answer "There is" is put the natural way in plain English.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ אֶל־הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ צִדְקִיָּ֑הוּ מֶה֩ חָטָ֨אתִֽי לְךָ֤ וְלַעֲבָדֶ֨יךָ֙ וְלָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה כִּֽי־נְתַתֶּ֥ם אוֹתִ֖י אֶל־בֵּ֥ית הַכֶּֽלֶא׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Jeremiah to the king Zedekiah: What have I sinned against you and against your servants and against the people this, that you have put me into [the] house of the prison?

en.L: And Jeremiah said to King Zedekiah, "How have I sinned against you or against your servants or against this people, that you have put me in the prison house?
en.B: Then Jeremiah said to King Zedekiah, "What wrong have I done to you or your officials or this people, that you have put me in prison?
en.R: Then Jeremiah said to King Zedekiah, "What crime have I committed against you, your officials or these people? Why have you put me in prison?

es.L: Y dijo Jeremías al rey Sedequías: «¿En qué he pecado contra ti, o contra tus siervos, o contra este pueblo, para que me hayan puesto en la casa de la cárcel?
es.B: Luego Jeremías le dijo al rey Sedequías: «¿Qué mal te he hecho a ti, o a tus funcionarios, o a este pueblo, para que me hayan metido en la cárcel?
es.R: Luego Jeremías le dijo al rey Sedequías: «¿Qué crimen he cometido contra ti, contra tus funcionarios o contra esta gente? ¿Por qué me han metido en la cárcel?

sw.L: Yeremia akamwambia mfalme Sedekia, "Nimekutenda dhambi gani wewe, au watumishi wako, au watu hawa, hata mkanitia katika nyumba ya gereza?
sw.B: Kisha Yeremia akamwambia mfalme Sedekia, "Nimekukosea nini wewe, au maafisa wako, au watu hawa, hata mkanitia gerezani?
sw.R: Kisha Yeremia akamwambia mfalme Sedekia, "Nimefanya kosa gani dhidi yako, maafisa wako au watu hawa? Kwa nini mmenitia gerezani?

decisions.choice: sinned against: wronged, given cause for punishment
decisions.reason: Here the verb has its legal sense, to be guilty of an offense against someone. Jeremiah asks what wrong he has done that could justify his imprisonment.

decisions.choice: you have put me: plural, the king and his court
decisions.reason: The verb is plural. Jeremiah holds the king and his officials together responsible for his imprisonment.

decisions.choice: servants (L); officials (B, R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for a king's court officials: "servants" at Literal, "officials" at Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: the quotation stays open
decisions.reason: Jeremiah's appeal runs to the end of verse 20, so the quotation mark opened here closes there.

decisions.choice: me hayan puesto / me han metido (they)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb is plural, "you (all) have put me", the king with his officials; Spanish says it with an impersonal third person plural, which reads the same in both forms of address.

decisions.choice: "mkanitia", "mmenitia" (plural "you")
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb is plural, the king and his court together; Swahili shows it in the verb.

source.text: וְאַיֵּה֙ נְבִ֣יאֵיכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־נִבְּא֥וּ לָכֶ֖ם לֵאמֹ֑ר לֹֽא־יָבֹ֤א מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶל֙ עֲלֵיכֶ֔ם וְעַ֖ל הָאָ֥רֶץ הַזֹּֽאת׃

records.literal_gloss: And where [are] your prophets who prophesied to you, saying: Not will come [the] king of Babylon against you and against the land this?

en.L: And where are your prophets who prophesied to you, saying, 'The king of Babylon will not come against you or against this land'?
en.B: Where are your prophets now, who prophesied to you that the king of Babylon would not come against you or against this land?
en.R: Where are your prophets now? They told you that the king of Babylon would not attack you or this land.

es.L: ¿Y dónde [están] {{plural_you:sus profetas|vuestros profetas}} que {{plural_you:les|os}} profetizaban, diciendo: “No vendrá el rey de Babilonia contra {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} ni contra esta tierra”?
es.B: ¿Dónde están ahora {{plural_you:sus profetas|vuestros profetas}}, que {{plural_you:les|os}} profetizaban que el rey de Babilonia no vendría contra {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} ni contra esta tierra?
es.R: ¿Dónde están ahora {{plural_you:sus profetas|vuestros profetas}}? Ellos {{plural_you:les|os}} decían que el rey de Babilonia no {{plural_you:los|os}} atacaría a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} ni a este país.

sw.L: Na wako wapi manabii wenu waliowatabiria, kusema, 'Mfalme wa Babeli hatakuja juu yenu wala juu ya nchi hii'?
sw.B: Wako wapi sasa manabii wenu waliowatabiria kwamba mfalme wa Babeli hatakuja kuwashambulia ninyi wala nchi hii?
sw.R: Wako wapi sasa manabii wenu? Waliwaambia kwamba mfalme wa Babeli hatawashambulia ninyi wala nchi hii.

decisions.choice: And where: the reading the scribes noted in the margin
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew text has a word that would mean "where is he?"; the scribes noted in the margin that it is to be read "and where". The sense is the same either way: a challenge to the king to produce the prophets who had promised safety.

decisions.choice: your prophets: the prophets who promised peace
decisions.reason: Prophets such as Hananiah had said the king of Babylon would soon be broken (28:2-4, 11; compare 14:13; 23:16-17; 27:14-16). Babylon has come, as Jeremiah said, and the lifting of the siege is only for a time (verse 8).

decisions.choice: your, you: plural
decisions.reason: Jeremiah speaks to the king and those around him: the prophets were their prophets, and the promise was made to them.

decisions.choice: now
decisions.reason: "Now" brings out the point of the question: the false prophets have been proved wrong by events.

decisions.choice: plural_you (sus profetas / vuestros profetas)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "your" and "you" are plural in this verse: Jeremiah turns from the king to the king with his court and people, who all trusted those prophets.

source.text: וְעַתָּ֕ה שְֽׁמַֽע־נָ֖א אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ תִּפָּל־נָ֤א תְחִנָּתִי֙ לְפָנֶ֔יךָ וְאַל־תְּשִׁבֵ֗נִי בֵּ֚ית יְהוֹנָתָ֣ן הַסֹּפֵ֔ר וְלֹ֥א אָמ֖וּת שָֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: And now listen please, my lord the king; let fall please my supplication before you, and do not make me return [to the] house of Jonathan the scribe, and not I will die there.

en.L: And now, please listen, my lord the king; please let my plea fall before you, and do not send me back to the house of Jonathan the secretary, so that I may not die there."
en.B: Now please listen, my lord the king. Please accept my plea: do not send me back to the house of Jonathan the secretary, or I will die there."
en.R: Now please listen to me, my lord the king. I beg you to do what I ask. Do not send me back to the house of Jonathan the secretary. If you do, I will die there."

es.L: Y ahora escucha, por favor, mi señor el rey; caiga, por favor, mi súplica delante de ti, y no me hagas volver a la casa de Jonatán el escriba, para que no muera yo allí».
es.B: Ahora, por favor, escucha, mi señor el rey. Te ruego que aceptes mi súplica: no me hagas volver a la casa de Jonatán el secretario, o moriré allí».
es.R: Ahora, por favor, escúchame, mi señor el rey. Te ruego que hagas lo que te pido. No me mandes de vuelta a la casa de Jonatán el secretario. Si lo haces, moriré allí».

sw.L: Basi sasa, sikiliza tafadhali, bwana wangu mfalme; tafadhali dua yangu ianguke mbele yako, wala usinirudishe katika nyumba ya Yonathani mwandishi, nisije nikafa huko."
sw.B: Basi sasa tafadhali sikiliza, bwana wangu mfalme. Tafadhali kubali ombi langu: usinirudishe katika nyumba ya Yonathani katibu, la sivyo nitakufa huko."
sw.R: Basi sasa tafadhali nisikilize, bwana wangu mfalme. Nakusihi unifanyie ninalokuomba. Usinirudishe katika nyumba ya Yonathani katibu. Ukinirudisha huko, nitakufa."

decisions.choice: let my plea fall before you: may my request be accepted
decisions.reason: A plea that "falls before" someone is laid before him and favorably received (the same phrase in 36:7; 42:2, 9).

decisions.choice: my lord the king: the respectful address of a subject
decisions.reason: Jeremiah speaks with the courtesy owed to a king, even while he protests his innocence.

decisions.choice: and I will not die there: the purpose of the request
decisions.reason: The clause gives the reason for the plea: if he is sent back, he expects to die in that prison.

decisions.choice: I beg you to do what I ask ... If you do, I will die there.
decisions.reason: Readable says what "let my plea fall before you" means and breaks the long request into short sentences.

source.text: וַיְצַוֶּ֞ה הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ צִדְקִיָּ֗הוּ וַיַּפְקִ֣דוּ אֶֽת־יִרְמְיָהוּ֮ בַּחֲצַ֣ר הַמַּטָּרָה֒ וְנָתֹן֩ ל֨וֹ כִכַּר־לֶ֤חֶם לַיּוֹם֙ מִח֣וּץ הָאֹפִ֔ים עַד־תֹּ֥ם כָּל־הַלֶּ֖חֶם מִן־הָעִ֑יר וַיֵּ֣שֶׁב יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ בַּחֲצַ֖ר הַמַּטָּרָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And commanded the king Zedekiah, and they committed Jeremiah in [the] court of the guard, and giving to him a round of bread for the day from [the] street of the bakers, until finished all the bread from the city. And remained Jeremiah in [the] court of the guard.

en.L: And King Zedekiah gave orders, and they committed Jeremiah to the court of the guard, and a loaf of bread was given to him each day from the bakers' street, until all the bread in the city was gone. And Jeremiah remained in the court of the guard.
en.B: So King Zedekiah gave orders, and Jeremiah was placed in the court of the guard. Each day he was given a loaf of bread from the street of the bakers, until there was no bread left in the city. And Jeremiah stayed in the court of the guard.
en.R: So King Zedekiah gave orders, and Jeremiah was kept in the courtyard of the palace guard. Every day he was given a loaf of bread from the street where the bakers worked, until all the bread in the city was used up. So Jeremiah stayed in the courtyard of the guard.

es.L: Y mandó el rey Sedequías, y pusieron a Jeremías en el patio de la guardia, y le daban una torta de pan cada día de la calle de los panaderos, hasta que se acabó todo el pan de la ciudad. Y quedó Jeremías en el patio de la guardia.
es.B: Entonces el rey Sedequías dio órdenes, y pusieron a Jeremías en el patio de la guardia. Cada día le daban una torta de pan de la calle de los panaderos, hasta que no quedó pan en la ciudad. Y Jeremías se quedó en el patio de la guardia.
es.R: Así que el rey Sedequías dio órdenes, y dejaron a Jeremías en el patio de la guardia del palacio. Todos los días le daban una torta de pan de la calle donde trabajaban los panaderos, hasta que se acabó todo el pan de la ciudad. Así que Jeremías se quedó en el patio de la guardia.

sw.L: Ndipo mfalme Sedekia akaamuru, nao wakamweka Yeremia katika ua wa walinzi, naye akapewa mkate mmoja kila siku kutoka katika mtaa wa waokaji, mpaka mikate yote ya mji ikaisha. Basi Yeremia akakaa katika ua wa walinzi.
sw.B: Basi mfalme Sedekia akatoa amri, naye Yeremia akawekwa katika ua wa walinzi. Kila siku alipewa mkate mmoja kutoka katika mtaa wa waokaji, mpaka mikate yote ikaisha mjini. Basi Yeremia akakaa katika ua wa walinzi.
sw.R: Basi mfalme Sedekia akatoa amri, naye Yeremia akawekwa katika ua wa walinzi wa ikulu. Kila siku alipewa mkate mmoja kutoka katika mtaa ambamo waokaji walifanya kazi, mpaka mikate yote ya mji ikaisha. Kwa hiyo Yeremia akakaa katika ua wa walinzi.

decisions.choice: the court of the guard: an open courtyard by the palace where prisoners were held
decisions.reason: It was a guarded enclosure attached to the royal palace (32:2). It was far less harsh than the cistern: there Jeremiah could receive visitors and do business (32:8-12).

decisions.choice: a loaf was given to him: a standing order
decisions.reason: The verb is an infinitive with no stated subject, describing a regular daily supply. The king provides for him without setting him free.

decisions.choice: until all the bread was gone: the famine at the end of the siege
decisions.reason: When the siege resumed, the food in the city ran out shortly before it fell (38:9; 52:6; 2 Kings 25:3).

decisions.choice: the bakers' street: the quarter where the bakers worked
decisions.reason: Ancient cities often had streets named after the trade carried on there.

decisions.choice: the courtyard of the palace guard
decisions.reason: Readable says "courtyard" and adds "palace" so that the reader can picture where Jeremiah was held.

decisions.choice: he was given
decisions.reason: The Hebrew's impersonal "giving" is put in the passive at every level; Literal keeps the order of the Hebrew clauses.

decisions.choice: el patio de la guardia
decisions.reason: "Patio" is used for this open court of the palace guard, as in 32:2 and through chapters 38-39; "atrio" stays for the temple courts.

decisions.choice: "ua wa walinzi" (L, B); "ua wa walinzi wa ikulu" (R)
decisions.reason: The court of the guard is named for the guards who kept it; Readable adds that it was by the palace, as the English Readable does.
